goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — The discarded async forEach callback lets rescheduling report success before calendar cleanup starts and makes import failures bypass the surrounding catch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that on line 125, the callback is changed to `async (bookingRef) => {` inside a `.forEach()`. Using async callbacks with forEach means the promises are not awaited - forEach ignores return values. This means: 1) The function will continue/complete before the async operations finish, 2) Any errors thrown inside the async callback won't be caught by the surrounding try/catch block since they occur in separate promise chains. The finding correctly identifies that this pattern allows the reschedule to report success before calendar cleanup completes and bypasses error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460 — Awaiting the adapter import inside an unobserved forEach callback lets recurring cancellation delete local references before the external calendar deletions are registered or started.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 458 that `forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })` is used. Using async callbacks with forEach means the promises are not awaited - forEach doesn't wait for async callbacks to complete. This means the loop will complete immediately while the calendar deletion operations are still pending. Combined with the fact that this is inside a larger async function, the local database operations could complete before the external calendar deletions finish or even start, leading to inconsistent state where local references are deleted but external calendar events remain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553 — The unawaited async forEach lets the mutation continue successfully while calendar deletion is still pending and turns lookup failures into unhandled rejections.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 553 that `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` is used with an async callback. The `forEach` method does not await the promises returned by async callbacks, meaning the calendar deletion operations (`calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will run in the background without being awaited. This is a real bug because: 1) The mutation will complete and return success before calendar deletions finish, 2) Any errors in the async callbacks become unhandled promise rejections rather than being caught by the surrounding try-catch, 3) The return statements inside forEach don't actually do anything useful since forEach ignores return values. This is a known anti-pattern with async/forEach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — Eagerly launching every import without rejection handlers lets a failure in any unused app become an unhandled rejection instead of propagating through the requested app

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff. The imports are NOT eagerly launched at module load time. The appStore object contains dynamic import expressions (import('./applecalendar'), etc.) which return Promises, but these Promises are only created when the property is accessed and awaited (e.g., 'await appStore[appName]'). The imports are lazy - they only execute when specifically requested. There's no eager launching of all imports that would cause unhandled rejections from unused apps.

When you pass an async function to forEach, the returned promises are discarded - forEach doesn't await them. This means: 1) The `await getCalendar()` call on line 128 will execute asynchronously but the surrounding try/catch block won't catch any rejections from these async callbacks, 2) Any errors from the calendar operations become unhandled promise rejections, 3) The code continues execution without waiting for the calendar deletions to complete. This is a real bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — Constructing the registry with immediate import() calls starts every app package load for each appStore consumer, retaining all-package startup and memory cost while adding chunk fan-out; store lazy loader functions and invoke only the selected app instead.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new implementation in packages/app-store/index.ts creates an object where each property is an immediate import() call (Promise). This means when appStore is first accessed, all dynamic imports are triggered simultaneously, loading all app packages into memory. The diff shows 'applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")' etc. for every app. While the code does work (callers now await the promises), the finding's point about startup/memory cost is valid - storing lazy loader functions like '() => import("./applecalendar")' would defer loading until actually needed. This is a legitimate architectural concern about the implementation approach, not a bug but an important design consideration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — Eagerly launching every import promise without rejection handlers lets any unused app-load failure become an unhandled rejection that can terminate the process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that appStore is now an object where each property is a Promise from dynamic import() (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). These promises are created immediately when the module loads, but they're only awaited later when accessed. If any of these imports fail (e.g., missing module, syntax error), the promise rejection would be unhandled at creation time since no .catch() is attached. This could cause unhandled rejection warnings or process termination depending on Node.js configuration, even for apps that are never used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460 — Add a deferred-import recurring-cancellation test because the async callbacks can leave apiDeletes empty when Promise.all consumes it and let the handler finish before deletions start.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the diff. At line 458, the code uses `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` which creates async callbacks that are not awaited. The `apiDeletes.push()` calls inside these callbacks may not execute before `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` is called later, because forEach doesn't wait for async callbacks to complete. This means the array could be empty or incomplete when Promise.all processes it, causing deletions to potentially not complete before the handler finishes. This is the same pattern issue seen in other files in this diff (vital/lib/reschedule.ts, wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, bookings.tsx) where forEach with async callbacks is used incorrectly.
